sections.title: Sales grew through bigger orders, not more of them
sections.metric_label: sales growth, Dec–Nov year on year
sections.finding: Merchandise sales reached £10.06M in the twelve months to November 2011, up 6.7% on the year before. Orders fell 4.0%, so all of the growth came from average order value, which rose 11.2%.
sections.action: Track order value by customer segment to confirm whether larger baskets come from existing wholesalers or a shift in customer mix.

sections.title: The business lives and dies by autumn
sections.finding: September to November delivered 36% of the year's sales. November 2011 alone was £1.46M, 1.5% above November 2010. Stock for the Christmas range has to be committed by late summer.
sections.action: Plan inventory and staffing around the Q4 ramp; this is where forecast accuracy pays most.

sections.title: A UK business with a few very large overseas accounts
sections.finding: The UK accounts for 86% of sales. Outside it, value is concentrated: 3 identified customers in Ireland bought £629k, with an average order of £1,082.
sections.action: Treat the top overseas accounts as key accounts with named owners; losing one is material.

sections.title: Orders arrive Monday to Friday lunchtime, plus Sunday
sections.finding: Thursday is the busiest day and 12:00 the busiest hour. Saturday trading is almost non-existent (30 orders in two years), while Sunday is a normal trading day.
sections.action: Align staffing with observed ordering hours. Test promotion timing separately before claiming it improves sales.

sections.title: A fifth of customers drive three quarters of revenue
sections.metric_label: of identified sales from the top 20% of customers
sections.finding: Champions are 1,508 customers (26%) but 71% of identified revenue. 397 'at risk' customers used to order often (median 5 orders) but have been quiet for 359 days; they spent £1.37M in total.
sections.action: Run a win-back campaign for the at-risk segment before spending on acquisition.

sections.title: Compare retention at the same cohort maturity
sections.metric_label: of new customers buy again the next month
sections.finding: Across 11 cohorts with twelve complete follow-up months, 20% ordered in month one and 18% in month twelve. These are monthly activity rates for the same cohorts, not the probability of staying after a second purchase. The initial left-censored cohort is excluded.
sections.action: Test an early reorder reminder against a control group; measure repeat orders and incremental value.

sections.title: A long tail of slow sellers
sections.finding: 1,024 of 4,707 products produce 80% of sales. The bottom 2,423 products ('C' class) share just 5%.
sections.action: Review C-class lines alongside margin, stock and range requirements before proposing delisting.

sections.title: Customers buy in matching sets
sections.metric_label: lift for the strongest product pair
sections.finding: The strongest pairing is Pink Polkadot Cup with Blue Polkadot Cup: bought together 521 times, 36 times more often than chance. Most top pairs are colour variants of the same item.
sections.action: Sell colour variants as bundles and place them together online.

sections.title: Large credit adjustments need separate investigation
sections.metric_label: of sales credited, excluding large adjustments
sections.finding: Credits below the size threshold total 2.2% of sales; including large adjustments, credits total 3.6%. Large adjustments account for £287k. The flag means at least 1,000 units or £10,000 per line; it does not prove a cancellation or physical return.
sections.action: Reconcile large credits to their original invoices before assigning a cause. Review sensitivity to the size threshold.

sections.title: Forecast accuracy on a separate holdout
sections.metric_label: less forecast error than a 4-week average
sections.finding: On a holdout of five forecast weeks before Christmas 2011, gradient boosting had a weighted error of 46% against 53% for a 4-week average. Its signed bias was -18%, and the nominal 80% quantile range held 75% of actual outcomes.
sections.action: Use the quantile range in a replenishment scenario. Safety stock requires lead times, service targets and inventory costs, which this dataset lacks.

sections.title: Recommendations: blend 'similar' with 'trending'
sections.metric_label: hit rate of a best-seller list
sections.finding: For returning customers, a top-10 list blending purchase similarity with current trends contained a product they went on to buy for the first time 44% of the time, against 18% for best sellers and 43% for trending alone, while covering 27% of the catalogue (trending: 3%).
sections.action: Use the hybrid for 'you may also like' and reorder emails; A/B test before claiming uplift.
